description: Scorched near black, embers banked in every crack. A Slagling's last warmth: it warms the blade and the hide behind it.
lore: Most hard pieces come off the ground and go into the bag. This one goes into a pocket, and a great many of them never come out of it again. It is scorched nearly black across the plates, dark red where the shell shows through, and the seams are still lit: a low orange banked down in the cracks that does not brighten, does not spread, and has never yet been seen to go out.

In a blade it is a poor bargain and the trade is honest about that. It warms the edge a little, and what the edge does is a little warmer, and that is the whole of it. Worn, it earns itself back on one afternoon in a hundred. It takes the worst out of a real fire, a spill off the black rock, a roof going up, and there is no drama in the doing: a person walks out of a thing they had no business walking out of, singed, complaining about their eyebrows.

There is a small quarrel about them and it is a fair one. A teller will point out that the thing in your pocket is warm, and will be warm in a hundred years, and has not in all that time held anybody's attention for a minute together, and that a fire is not warmth, it is warmth with somebody talking beside it, and the two ought not to be confused by people who know better. The ones who carry them do not really disagree. They say only that high on the black rock, where the rota lapsed further back than anyone can now date and the nearest tended fire is a day's walk down the mountain, a warm thing in the pocket is not an argument about anything. It is company.
